pageCache.pageTitle: Stoke Park Infant School - Head Teacher's Welcome
pageCache.text:
Head Teacher's Welcome
I am delighted to welcome you to Stoke Park Infant School and to our school website. We are a busy three-form entry infant school with lots of exciting learning happening each day.
Our website will give you a taster of what life is like at our school, but for a fuller picture please come and see us!!!
At Stoke Park we all work together to ensure that our children develop life-long learning skills. Our school aims to ensure that the learning journey that the children are taking is an exciting one, with lots of fun, has high expectations, but allows each child to be an individual.
We aim for all our children to be:
Confident Individuals
Responsible Citizens
All the learning in school is based around the children's interests to ensure their engagement. We also have lots of opportunities to enrich the learning with surprises, visits, performances and visitors to keep the learning alive.
Our doors to children open at 8.45 and the school day ends at 3.20. However, wrap-around care is available through our external provider Sprouts. Breakfast club runs from 7.30-8.45am and the after-school club runs from 3.20 - 6.00pm. More information can be found by following the link below.

We aim to provide our children with an irresistible curriculum that encourages them to be Inspired, Challenged, Engaged and Enjoy their learning so that ...
We are Growing and Learning Together.......... To Be the Best we Can Be
I look forward to meeting you.
Mrs Emma-Jane Charles

Visions & Values
At Stoke Park Infant School we value every child as an individual and recognise that learning is not just about reading, writing and maths. We endeavour to support children in all aspects of their growth, including emotional, spiritual, cultural, moral as well as the full curriculum.
To support children and their families, we have a school ELSA (Emotional Literacy Support Adult) as well as a Home-School Link Worker. They are available to support families with specific needs and can be contacted via the school office.
Please visit the Support for Families & Pupils Page Here
Visions & Values

pageCache.pageTitle: Stoke Park Infant School - Wrap Around Care
pageCache.text:
Wrap Around Care
Working in Partnership with Stoke Park Infant and Junior School
Sprouts have been providing wrap-around care to schools within the local area of Locks Heath, since 2015. We are very excited to have expanded our portfolio into the Eastleigh area, and to be working with Stoke Park Infant and Junior School.
The club opened in September 2025, and we have built a good working relationship with both the school and families.
A little bit about us……
Sprouts’ founders Charlotte and Amy are qualified early years professionals who have worked in childcare for over 13 years whilst bringing up young families of their own, so share a wealth of skills and experience in the sector.
Currently working with over 900 children and their families within nine popular schools. Sprouts is dedicated to supporting schools and parents by providing specialist expertise and support in wrap-around care and holiday clubs.
Sprouts operate an online booking service, to make it flexible for families to book in advance or on the day.
To register and reserve your space, please book at www.sproutschildcare.co.uk
07:30 – start of school day
£7.00 per child per session
End of school day – 18:00
£13.50 per child per session
Find out more about us at www.sproutschildcare.co.uk

pageCache.pageTitle: Stoke Park Infant School - New Starters Year R ~ September 2027
pageCache.text:
New Starters Year R ~ September 2027
We would like to welcome parents to visit our school to meet with the headteacher, staff and children. This is an opportunity for you to see our school and find out more about us. The presentations are for adults, and would not be suitable for children. There will be opportunities for you to bring your child into school as part of their induction in the Summer Term. Please contact the school to book your place on any of the following dates:
Wednesday 7th October 2026 at 9.15am
Monday 19th October 2026 at 1.30pm
Wednesday 4th November 2026 at 9.15am
Thursday 26th November 2026 at 1.30pm
Tuesday 8th December 2026 at 9.15am
Thursday 7th January 2027 at 1.30pm
To book your place on any of these dates, please contact the school office on 02380 601773
Starting school is an important stage in your child’s development and, although September 2027 is a long way off, now is the time to think about choosing a school for your child.
At Stoke Park Infant School we aim for every child to be: a successful learner who enjoys learning, makes progress and achieves; a confident individual who is able to lead a safe, healthy and fulfilling life; and an international citizen who makes a positive contribution to society.
If you are considering applying for a place at Stoke Park Infant School, we would love you to visit and see the school in action. Please contact the school office and arrange for a school tour or presentation. If you are unable to join a tour, then please feel free to contact the headteacher for a virtual chat or a phone call.
If you have specific questions about your child starting school and would like to speak with a member of the school team, then please do not hesitate to contact the office, and we shall pass your enquiry onto the relevant member of staff.
Further information about school admissions can be found on Hampshire County Council’s website www.hants.gov.uk/admissions.
If you are considering applying for a place, I look forward to welcoming you to Stoke Park Infant School.
Mrs Emma – Jane Charles
New Starters Year R ~ September 2027

pageCache.text:
Governing Body
Stoke Park Infant School's governing body follows a flat structure and meets at least each half-term to discuss all aspects of governance.
The Department for Education guidance states that diversity of data, relating to the members of the governing body, should be widely accessible to members of the school community and the public. As this is non-statutory, the governing body is awaiting further guidance before publishing this information.
Vacancies
We currently have vacancies for 4 co-opted governors. If you are interested in either of these roles, please contact our clerk to the governing body, Karen Roebuck, addressed to adminoffice@stokepark-inf.hants.sch.uk in the first instance.
Governing Body Meeting Minutes
Full governing body minutes are available on request from the School Office.

Clubs
The school offers a mixture of clubs, run by either external providers or in house by staff. We offer the following by external providers:
Showstoppers - This is a club that offers children the opportunity to 'perform' - great for any budding actors and performers!
RockSteady - Calling all rock and pop band performers - learn an instrument or sing - you can create your own band and learn musical instruments, including electric guitar, drums or keyboard. You can then perform in your band at an end of term concert!
Karate - Sama Karate is taught as an external club where the children can learn karate skills and improve their skills in a grading
All teachers run clubs on a Wednesday from 3.20 -4.20pm and are £20 per term. Each term we change the focus and these are offered to all children in KS1.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stoke Park Infant School - Colour Monsters (Year R/1)
pageCache.text:
Colour Monsters (Year R/1)
At Stoke Park Infant school, we use The Colour Monster approach to help children recognise, understand and manage their emotions. Based on the popular story by Anna Llenas, the Colour Monster uses different colours to represent different feelings, making emotions easier for children to identify and talk about.
Black = Worried or Scared
Multicoloured = Confused
Children are encouraged to check in on their feelings throughout the day, using the Colour Monster language to express how they are feeling. This supports the development of emotional vocabulary, self-awareness and emotional regulation skills.
By helping children recognise their emotions and understand that all feelings are normal and valid, we can support them in choosing appropriate strategies to regulate their emotions, build resilience and develop positive relationships with others.
The Colour Monster approach is used consistently throughout Year R and continues into Year 1, providing children with a familiar and accessible way to understand and express their feelings. As pupils progress through the school, this learning is built upon through the Zones of Regulation programme, which develops their understanding of emotions, self-regulation and wellbeing using age-appropriate language and strategies. This ensures a consistent and progressive approach to supporting children's emotional development across the school.

pageCache.pageTitle: Stoke Park Infant School - Supporting Children & Families
pageCache.text:
Supporting Children & Families
The ELSA programme aims to promote emotional wellbeing in children and support the child to use a variety of strategies to help them solve their problems independently.
Emotional Literacy support involves identifying specific targets which the pupil works through, with the support of the ELSA in school.
The ELSA will work closely with the class teacher to ensure the child has continued support in the class.
The ELSA has taken a training course and is lead and managed by Hampshire and The Isle of Wight Educational Psychology Department.
Supporting Children & Families
At Stoke Park Infant School we have a Home School Link Worker who is available to listen and support on many parenting strategies to help you.
The Home-School Link Worker is here to support children and their families in lots of ways.
*Talking, listening and supporting, including 1-1 work with parents, carers and children.
*Aiming to find strategies to help parents, carers and children to improve learning, behaviour and relationships.
*Signposting and referring to local services.
